name: secret-capture-request
description: Mint a one-time, single-use, 30-minute link the user can click to enter a personal secret (e.g. a website password). The value is typed into a secure web form and written straight to the vault under a deterministic `user.*` key — repeat captures of the same secret update that key in place instead of minting a new slug. Call list-user-secrets first; if a matching key already exists, pass that exact name as secret_name. You never see the value — this skill returns only the link. Relay the returned capture_url to the user verbatim. When the user fills the link, you are automatically brought back into this conversation to continue.

inputs.secret_name: string (human description of the secret, e.g. 'twitter password'; canonicalized to user.<slug>. Pass an exact existing user.* key from list-user-secrets to update that key in place)
inputs.label: string? (text shown to the user on the form; defaults to the secret_name)
inputs.resume_intent: string? (a short description of what you are trying to do, e.g. 'check the user's Aeroplan balance'; surfaced back to you when the secret is captured so you can continue)

outputs.capture_url: string (the one-time link to send the user)
outputs.expires_at: string (local ISO timestamp when the link expires)
outputs.secret_name: string (the resolved user.<slug> vault key the value will be stored under)
outputs.reused_existing: boolean (true when this capture will update an already-stored user.* key)
